http://www.euronews.com/2026/08/13/who-i.text: One of the founding figures of Iran's IRGC Mohsen Rezaei has been appointed secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council — giving one of the country's most controversial senior figures formal authority over the institution responsible for Tehran's strategic decisions.The appointment was made in a presidential decree signed by Masoud Pezeshkian on Sunday.Hours earlier, Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei had separately appointed Rezaei as his personal representative on the council.With nearly five decades at the top of the Islamic Republic's security and military apparatus, Rezaei, 71, succeeds Mohammad Bagher Zolghadr, a veteran IRGC commander who resigned after around four months in the post and was appointed as a political adviser to Khamenei.Right after his appointment was announced, Rezaei has said publicly that Iran will not open a second shipping corridor in the Strait of Hormuz, that US warships entering the strait will be targeted, and that the war must end and Iran's frozen assets must be released before Hormuz can be reopened.Who is Mohsen Rezaei?Rezaei, whose birth name was Sabzvar, was born in 1954 in Khuzestan province into a Bakhtiari tribal family.Initially a political activist against the rule of Shah Reza Pahlavi in the early 1970s, Rezaei was arrested by the shah's intelligence agency SAVAK and imprisoned in Ahvaz.He was one of the founders of the Mansouroun militant group, which helped lay the groundwork for the Mojahedin of the Islamic Revolution Organisation.After the 1979 revolution, Rezaei joined the central council of the Islamic Republic and served on a 12-member committee that drafted the IRGC's constitution.In September 1981, at the age of 27, Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini appointed him commander-in-chief of the Revolutionary Guards.Rezaei held the position for 16 years — making him one of the longest-serving military commanders in the history of the Islamic Republic — before stepping down in September 1997.He then became secretary of the Expediency Discernment Council, the body that resolves disputes between parliament and the Guardian Council and sets broad state policy, for nearly 24 years.He was appointed deputy president for economy under President Ebrahim Raisi in 2021, a post he left in June 2023.Despite this record of institutional prominence, Rezaei has run for president four times and lost each time. In the 2021 election, he received 3.4 million votes — fewer than the number of ballots deemed invalid in the vote.The bombing of the Jewish centre in ArgentinaRezaei's name has been associated internationally with the 1994 bombing of the AMIA Jewish community centre in Buenos Aires, which killed 85 people and injured hundreds in the deadliest terrorist attack in Argentina's history.In 2007, Argentine prosecutors sought arrest warrants for nine people in connection with the attack, including Rezaei, then IRGC commander. Interpol issued a Red Notice against him that remains in force.Tehran and Rezaei have consistently denied any involvement in the attack, describing the allegations as politically motivated.The case has nevertheless had practical consequences: Argentina protested his appointment as deputy economic president in 2021, previously objected to his attendance at the inaugurations of Nicaraguan presidents, and asked Qatar to arrest and extradite him during a visit to Doha — a request that was not carried out.Operation Karbala-4The most controversial episode of Rezaei's military command domestically was Operation Karbala-4, a December 1986 assault during the Iraq-Iran war intended to retake parts of the Faw area that was detected and repelled by Iraqi forces, resulting in heavy Iranian casualties, including frogmen units.In 2015, the remains of 175 divers who had participated in the operation, reportedly buried with their hands tied, were discovered and identified.Rezaei's subsequent claim that continuing the operation after it had been compromised was a deliberate deception ahead of the larger Operation Karbala-5 — or the siege of Basra, the largest military offensive of the war — drew sharp criticism from former officials, journalists and social media users.Qassem Soleimani, then Quds Force commander, contradicted the account by saying Karbala-4 had been the primary operation all along.Another controversy surfaced in November 2011, when Rezaei's eldest son Ahmad, who had previously defected to the US and given media interviews criticising senior Islamic Republic officials, was found dead in a Dubai hotel room.Dubai police attributed the death to an overdose of antidepressants. Rezaei's family and the Expediency Council secretariat rejected that conclusion and described the death as suspicious. The cause of Ahmad Rezaei's death has never been conclusively established.War, succession and regime in fluxRezaei's appointment comes after one of the most turbulent periods in the Islamic Republic's history.The US and Israel launched broad strikes against Iranian military targets on 28 February, killing Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, Defence Minister Mohammad Reza Ashtiani and around 40 senior military and security commanders.Ali Larijani, who had been secretary of the Supreme National Security Council since August 2025 and was regarded by many analysts as Iran's most powerful figure on the eve of the war, was killed in a subsequent wave of Israeli strikes on Tehran.Zolghadr then succeeded Larijani in that role. Under the constitution, an interim council of President Pezeshkian, judiciary chief Gholam-Hossein Mohseni Ejei and a Guardian Council-appointed cleric managed the country's leadership functions until Mojtaba Khamenei was selected as the third ayatollah on 9 March.

https://telex.hu/gazdasag/2026/09/18/dun.text: Menü Kereső Visszafizette a Duna Aszfalt az afrikai projektjéhez nyújtott kölcsönt az Eximbanknak és az MFB Banknak Gazdaság Iván-Nagy Szilvia Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom Teljes egészében visszafizette az Eximbanknak és az MFB Banknak az afrikai Kasomeno–Mwenda projekthez kapcsolódó kötvények összegét a Duna Aszfalt, az összes kamattal együtt – tájékoztatta az MTI-t pénteken a vállalat. A Duna Aszfalt közleménye szerint 2025 novembere óta a vállalat több mint 10 milliárd forint kamatot fizetett az állami tulajdonú bankoknak. A Gazdasági és Energetikai Minisztérium július végén tett feljelentést a Duna Aszfalt kongói–zambiai beruházásának állami finanszírozása miatt. A Duna Aszfalt közleménye szerint a kölcsön visszafizetésével lezárult a projekt közvetett állami finanszírozása, és megszűnt az ahhoz kapcsolódó állami kezesség is. Ez, hangsúlyozták, azt jelenti, hogy a Kasomeno–Mwenda projekthez kapcsolódóan a magyar államot a jövőben nem terheli semmilyen pénzügyi kockázat. A közlemény szerint a Duna Group a magyar állam korábbi finanszírozási konstrukcióval kapcsolatos álláspontját figyelembe véve kezdeményezte a kötvények önkéntes visszaváltását. A kötvények visszaváltása nem érinti a beruházás megvalósítását: a GED Africa projekt jelenleg 40 százalékos készültségen áll, és stabil pénzügyi háttérrel, a tervek szerint halad tovább. A Duna Group értékelése szerint a kötvények visszaváltása egyértelmű és kiszámítható helyzetet teremt a projekt nemzetközi partnerei számára. A Duna Group számára különösen fontos, hogy egy ilyen jelentőségű nemzetközi beruházás stabil környezetben valósuljon meg, és a projekt körüli pénzügyi kérdések ne befolyásolják sem a vállalatcsoport, sem Magyarország nemzetközi üzleti hitelességét és jó hírnevét – áll a közleményben. A tájékoztatás arra is kitér, hogy a Duna Group minden vitatott pontban nyert a GED Africa Limited egyik tulajdonosa által 2024 júliusában indított nemzetközi jogvitában. Az eljárás a GED Africa Limitedre vonatkozó szindikátusi szerződés egyes kérdéseit érintette. A Nemzetközi Kereskedelmi Kamara (ICC) választottbírósága 2026 szeptemberében meghozott döntésében az eljárás valamennyi érdemi kérdésében a Duna Group álláspontjának megfelelően határozott, ezzel a jogvita teljes egészében lezárult. A Kasomeno–Mwenda infrastruktúra-fejlesztési projekt a Kongói Demokratikus Köztársaság és Zambia között teremt új közlekedési és kereskedelmi kapcsolatot. A 25 éves együttműködés keretében közel 184 kilométernyi közúti infrastruktúra, egy 362 méteres új ferdekábeles híd, két korszerű határállomás, valamint elektronikus útdíjszedési és üzemeltetési rendszer valósul meg. A közlemény kiemeli, hogy az új út egy világkereskedelmi jelentőségű kereskedelmi folyosó része, amely a stratégiai nyersanyagokban gazdag közép-afrikai rézövezetet kapcsolja össze Tanzánia Dar es Salaam kikötőjével és ezen keresztül a világpiaccal. Az új kapcsolat mintegy 500 kilométerrel rövidíti le a fuvarozási útvonalat, és drasztikusan csökkenti a várakozási időt a határon. Magyar Péter miniszterelnök egy a Facebook-oldalán augusztus 25-én közzétett videóban nehezményezte, hogy két állami bank az Orbán-kormány alatt 126 milliárd forintnyi kötvényt jegyzett le a rendkívül kockázatos afrikai ügylet során, ráadásul úgy, hogy a finanszírozás mintegy 80 százalékára a magyar állam kezességet vállalt. Hozzátette, mindez egy olyan beruházás esetében történt, amely a legmagasabb országkockázati kategóriába sorolt államokhoz kapcsolódott. A kormányfő beszámolt arról is, hogy a Duna Aszfalt alig néhány héttel a feljelentés után bejelentette, névértéken, kamatokkal együtt visszaváltja ezeket a kötvényeket. https://www.politico.eu/article/emmanuel.text: PARIS — French President Emmanuel Macron has instructed local authorities to ban protests on Saturday except those organized by unions, he said Thursday. Any request to “protest” or “regroup” made by people “who have no legitimacy to do so” will be “refused,” Macron said after a security meeting with Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu and intelligence services. The aim, he added, is to maintain public order and “protect businesses” after last week’s turmoil in France. Advertisement Advertisement Hundreds of thousands of demonstrators took to the streets, while incidents of vandalism and looting affected thousands of businesses and public buildings on the sidelines of the protests. Calls for a fresh round of protests have already begun to emerge online, raising the possibility of a protest movement that becomes a weekly occurrence, as was the case during the 2018-2019 Yellow Vest movement. “The president believes that six months before a presidential election, debate should take place more in TV studios, in newspapers, and ultimately by the choice at the ballot box,” a person close to the French president said. Trade unions usually hold talks with local authorities ahead of planned demonstrations. For Saturday, authorities may offer “alternative routes” to ensure maximum security, Macron announced. He added that he will chair a defense council Friday and announce “new decisions” afterward. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said elite tactical police units and a military unit normally deployed on French soil for counterterrorism operations would also be mobilized this weekend. Advertisement Advertisement The government has been accused of mismanaging last week’s protests by significantly underestimating the number of demonstrators and consequently failing to deploy enough police to prevent criminal acts on the sidelines. A protest organized by a major trade union Saturday in Paris has been approved, French media reported , while all protests in the area including Lyon, one of the country’s biggest cities, have been banned .
